senses.gloss: Basic knowledge of and skill in a particular subject.
examples: The high school added a required course in financial *literacy*.
Digital *literacy* is expected in almost every office job now.
The museum's summer program builds science *literacy* in middle schoolers.

senses.gloss: One of the stores or offices that a business operates.
examples: The chain just opened its fortieth *location* in Ohio.
Both *locations* are closed on Sundays.
Our downtown *location* has a lot more parking than this one.

senses.gloss: A real place away from the studio where a movie or show is filmed.
examples: The whole third season was shot on *location* in New Mexico.
Scouts spent a month finding *locations* for the chase scene.
Filming on *location* costs more than building the set indoors.

senses.gloss: Angry disagreement, used only in the phrase at loggerheads.
senses.ru: разлад, ссора (в обороте at loggerheads — в контрах)
examples: The governor and the legislature are at *loggerheads* over the budget.
The two departments have been at *loggerheads* for years.
Negotiators are still at *loggerheads* about overtime pay.

senses.gloss: The worst or least impressive moments of an event or a period.
examples: The late show replayed the season's *lowlights* with a laugh track.
His whole speech was a string of *lowlights*.
She walked the board through the quarter's highlights and *lowlights*.

senses.gloss: A person in stories who has real magical powers.
examples: In the book, a *magician* turns the prince into a bear.
The kingdom's *magicians* guarded a stone that granted wishes.
He read every fantasy novel about dragons and *magicians*.

senses.gloss: A strong personal charm that draws people to someone.
examples: The candidate has a *magnetism* that no poll can measure.
Even on a bad night, his stage *magnetism* filled the room.
Her personal *magnetism* made strangers trust her right away.

senses.gloss: The act of keeping something going or holding it at a certain level.
examples: The treaty is about the *maintenance* of peace along the border.
Losing the weight was easy; *maintenance* is the hard part.
The city is responsible for the *maintenance* of order during the parade.

senses.gloss: A complete change in the look of a place, product, or organization.
examples: The kitchen got a *makeover* over the summer.
The airline gave its logo and cabins a *makeover*.
Two of the branch offices are due for *makeovers* next year.

senses.gloss: The process of dealing with or controlling a problem, resource, or condition.
examples: The clinic offers a free class on pain *management*.
Poor time *management* is why the project slipped a month.
The county's waste *management* costs have doubled since 2019.

senses.gloss: A clever move made to gain an advantage.
examples: The buyout was a legal *maneuver* to avoid the tax.
Both parties tried the same procedural *maneuvers* on the floor.
Getting the mayor onto the committee was a smart *maneuver*.

senses.gloss: Skillful handling or working of something with the hands or with tools.
examples: The surgery requires careful *manipulation* of very small instruments.
The chiropractor used gentle *manipulation* of the spine.
The software is built for fast *manipulation* of huge image files.

senses.gloss: An old book or document written out by hand.
examples: The library keeps a medieval *manuscript* in a climate-controlled case.
Monks copied *manuscripts* by candlelight.
The exhibit includes an illuminated *manuscript* from the 1300s.

senses.gloss: Any long, tiring activity or event that goes on and on.
examples: We watched a *marathon* of old sitcoms on Thanksgiving.
The budget hearing turned into a nine-hour *marathon*.
Finals week is a *marathon*, not a sprint.

senses.gloss: A false show put on to hide the truth.
examples: Their friendly lunches were a *masquerade*.
He kept up the *masquerade* of being a rich investor for two years.
The audit ended the company's *masquerade* of profitability.

senses.gloss: A completely one-sided defeat in a game or contest.
examples: The second half was a *massacre*.
Nobody expected such a *massacre* in the season opener.
The last two games were *massacres*, 42-3 and 38-7.

senses.gloss: Facts, ideas, or writing gathered for use in a book, class, or performance.
examples: The comedian is trying out new *material* at small clubs.
He spent a year in the archives collecting *material* for the biography.
The teacher posts all the course *materials* online.

senses.gloss: Cloth or fabric.
examples: She bought three yards of *material* for the curtains.
The dress is pretty, but the *material* wrinkles if you sit down.
Heavy *materials* like canvas are harder to sew on a home machine.

senses.gloss: The time when a loan, bond, or insurance policy comes due to be paid.
examples: The bond reaches *maturity* in ten years.
You'll pay a penalty for cashing the CD before *maturity*.
The notes have different *maturities*, from one year to thirty.

senses.gloss: A small round slice of meat or fish served as a portion.
examples: The special was pork *medallions* in a mustard sauce.
She seared the beef *medallions* two minutes a side.
Each *medallion* is wrapped in bacon before it goes in the oven.

senses.gloss: A piece of writing or speech that reflects deeply on a subject.
examples: The novel is a *meditation* on grief and memory.
His last album is a quiet *meditation* on getting older.
The essay reads like a *meditation* rather than an argument.
